title: Cloud Resource Tag Coverage Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:config:notification` events with `configRuleName="*required-tags*" complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.21 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:config:notification` traffic without `configRuleName="*required-tags*" complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT"`. Confirm UC-4.4.21 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:config:notification` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure inputs, GCP inputs; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" configRuleName="*required-tags*" complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.21_cloud_resource_tag_cover_21"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.4.21 — Cloud Resource Tag Coverage Trending: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:config:notification` for search criteria `configRuleName="*required-tags*" complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), missing governance tags for 'Cloud Resource Tag Coverage Trending' break cost allocation, environment scoping, and incident routing—delaying containment when resources cannot be classified quickly. UC-4.4.21 drives medium-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable AWS Config rule `required-tags` (or custom rule). Use Azure Policy for tag compliance. Export GCP Asset Inventory to BigQuery or Pub/Sub. Ingest compliance results in Splunk with normalized fields (provider, resource_type, compliance_status). For multi-cloud, use `index=cloud` and union searches per provider. Dashboard untagged resources by provider, resource type, and owner. Alert when critical resources (e.g. production EC2, storage) lack required tags (Environment, Owner, CostCenter).
visualization: Table (provider, resource type, compliance count), Pie chart (compliant vs non-compliant), Bar chart (non-compliant by tag key).
knownFalsePositives: Inventories can skip a run when an API is throttled or a connector is in maintenance, which looks like a big drop. We check the ingest time and the last good snapshot before we call it shrinkage.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure inputs, GCP inputs with the modular input for `aws:config:notification`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable AWS Config rule `required-tags` (or custom rule). Use Azure Policy for tag compliance. Export GCP Asset Inventory to BigQuery or Pub/Sub. Ingest compliance results in Splunk with normalized fields (provider, resource_type, compliance_status). For multi-cloud, use `index=cloud` and union searches per provider. Dashboard untagged resources by provider, resource type, and owner. Alert when critical resources (e.g. production EC2, storage) lack required tags (Environment, Owner, CostCenter).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" configRuleName="*required-tags*" complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.21_cloud_resource_tag_cover_21"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:notification` in `index=aws` to detect cloud resource tag coverage trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_21_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (provider, resource type, compliance count), Pie chart (compliant vs non-compliant), Bar chart (non-compliant by tag key)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure inputs, GCP inputs and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud resource tag coverage trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
